paragraphs: Here's what I want you to carry out of this one, friend. Mary hears the angel's word, and then she hurries, and Elizabeth says, "Blessed is she who has believed that the Lord’s word to her will be fulfilled." (Luke 1:45) Believing what God said is a batch anybody can bake, because believing is something God asks of every one of us.

Now listen to what Mary sings. She says God "has looked with favor on the humble state of His servant," and that "the Mighty One has done great things for me." (Luke 1:48-49) She doesn't point at herself, she says "My soul magnifies the Lord," and that's the whole point (Luke 1:46). When God does something great in your life, the song is about HIM, friend, and I have to remind myself of that every time somebody compliments my cookies.

And look at WHO God is in her song. He "has brought down rulers from their thrones, but has exalted the humble," and He remembered to be merciful "as He promised to our fathers, to Abraham and his descendants forever." (Luke 1:52, 54-55) So God keeps His promises, even the old ones, even when the world is looking the other way, and you can trust His word today for the same reason Mary did. And this story isn't over, friend, because that promise is still on its way to the cooling rack.
